{{Short description|Japanese mathematician}}
{{For|the novelist and military historian|Kaoru Ohno}}
'''Kaoru Ono''' (小野 薫, ''Ono Kaoru'', born 1962) is a Japanese mathematician, specializing in [[symplectic geometry]]. He is a professor at the [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (RIMS) at [[Kyoto University]].<ref name=RIMS>{{cite web|title=Ono, Kaoru|website=Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Kyoto University|url=http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/en/list/ono.html}}</ref>

Ono received from the University of [[Tokyo]] his undergraduate degree in 1984, his master's degree in 1987, and his Ph.D. in 1990.<ref>entry 000000236193 in the ''[https://dbr.nii.ac.jp/infolib/meta_pub/G0000016GAKUI1 Doctoral Dissertation Bibliographic Database] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150816064039/http://dbr.nii.ac.jp/infolib/meta_pub/G0000016GAKUI1 |date=2015-08-16 }}'' of the National Institute of Informatics {{in lang|ja}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author = Kaoru Ono | title = Equivariant index of Dirac operators | journal = Tohoku Mathematical Journal | volume = 42 | number = 3 | year = 1990 | pages = 319–332 | doi = 10.2748/tmj/1178227613 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Within symplectic geometry, his research has focused on [[Floer homology|Floer theory]] and holomorphic symplectic geometry involving [[holomorphic curve]]s and [[pseudoholomorphic curve]]s and their applications. He has collaborated extensively with [[Kenji Fukaya]], [[Yong-Geun Oh]], and Hiroshi Ohta (see [[Fukaya category]]).

{{blockquote|In a joint work with K. Fukaya, he constructed Floer cohomology of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on arbitrary closed symplectic manifolds as well as Gromov-Witten invariants. Using Novikov-Floer cohomology, he proved the <math>C^1</math>-flux conjecture. In recent years, he has been collaborating with Fukaya, Oh and Ohta in Floer theory for Lagrangian submanifolds and its implications in symplectic geometry and [[homological mirror symmetry]].<ref name=RIMS/>}}

Ono was awarded by the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]] in 1999 the [[Geometry prize|Geometry Prize]] and in 2005 the Autumn Prize.<ref>{{MacTutor|class=Honours|id=Autumn_Prize|title=The Autumn Prize of the Mathematical Society of Japan}}</ref> He was a 2006 recipient of the Inoue Prize of the Inoue Foundation for Science.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inoue-zaidan.or.jp/cmsdesigner/dlfile.php?entryname=f&entryid=00001&fileid=00000012&/vol.01-vol.40_%B3%D8%BD%D1%BE%DE%BC%F5%BE%DE%BC%D4.pdf|title=List of the 1st to 40th Academic Prize winners of the Inoue Prize|publisher=Inoue Foundation for Science|language=ja|access-date=2025-03-25}}</ref> In 2006 he was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Development in symplectic Floer theory'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Madrid]].

In 2022, he serves as Director of the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences of [[Kyoto University]] (KURIMS).
